title: Protocol for Inducing Hippocampal Formation Lesions in Japanese Quail
author: Damphousse, Miller, et al.

steps.title: Determine lesion coordinates
steps.instruction: Using the Baylé et al. (1974) atlas, set target coordinates: for hippocampal (Hp) lesions span 5 mm anterior to bregma to 3 mm posterior, 1.5 mm lateral on each side of the interfrontal suture, depth 3 mm; for area parahippocampalis (APH) lesions span 5 mm anterior to bregma to 3 mm posterior, 1.5–3.5 mm lateral to bregma, depth 2 mm.

steps.title: Sterilize instruments and workspace
steps.instruction: Autoclave all surgical instruments, sterilize between subjects with a bead sterilizer, and decontaminate surfaces with 75 % ethanol in addition to bead sterilization.

steps.title: Weigh and inject drugs
steps.instruction: Weigh each quail, then inject subcutaneously 5 mg kg⁻¹ analgesic and 5 mg kg⁻¹ antibiotic (calculate volume = weight (kg) × dose (mg kg⁻¹) ÷ concentration (mg mL⁻¹)); inject under the wing where skin is visible.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the quail in an induction chamber and deliver isoflurane 5 % in 500 mL min⁻¹ oxygen for induction.

steps.title: Position in stereotaxic
steps.instruction: When the righting reflex ceases, transfer the quail to a stereotaxic apparatus in prone position, secure ear bars (average insertion 1.2 cm) and the beak in a nose‑cone, and maintain body temperature at 35–40 °C with a heating pad (do not exceed 40 °C).

steps.title: Maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Continue isoflurane delivery at 5 % for induction and 2–3 % for maintenance in 225 mL min⁻¹ oxygen; monitor depth and adjust concentration if the animal moves, eyes open, or shows respiratory depression or cyanosis.

steps.title: Prepare surgical site
steps.instruction: Pluck feathers from the scalp area with forceps, inject 1 mL of 2 % lidocaine subcutaneously at the incision site, apply ophthalmic ointment to both eyes (reapply throughout surgery), and cover the body with a clear plastic shroud leaving only the head exposed.

steps.title: Disinfect skin
steps.instruction: Clean the surgical area sequentially with an antibacterial cleanser, isopropyl alcohol, and chlorhexidine gluconate solution; repeat the three‑step cleaning twice.

steps.title: Make scalp incision
steps.instruction: Incise the midline scalp to expose the skull and secure the skin edges with hemostats.

steps.title: Locate landmarks and mark window
steps.instruction: Clear skull fluid with cotton swabs, locate bregma and the interfrontal suture, then mark the rectangular craniotomy window on the skull using the predetermined coordinates (score the skull with a rotary‑tool bit or an unlacquered pencil). For bilateral APH lesions make two identical windows; Hp requires a single midline window.

steps.title: Drill and remove bone flap
steps.instruction: Using a rotary tool, drill the perimeter of the marked window gradually, keeping elbows planted on the table; remove the cut bone piece with forceps and clear any fragments with sterile saline.

steps.title: Prepare aspiration pipette
steps.instruction: Mark the desired lesion depth on a Pasteur pipette (3 mm for Hp, 2 mm for APH) with a permanent marker, sterilize the pipette in the bead sterilizer, and gently hook a needle tip to lift the dura from the brain surface.

steps.title: Aspirate target tissue
steps.instruction: Attach a bulb to the pipette, create suction by releasing air and pinching the valve, then aspirate brain tissue within the craniotomy to the depth marked on the pipette; control any bleeding with sterile cotton swabs or a hemostatic sponge before proceeding.

steps.title: Place hemostatic sponge
steps.instruction: Insert a sterile hemostatic sponge into the craniotomy, fitting it snugly to cover the exposed brain.

steps.title: Seal craniotomy with bone wax
steps.instruction: Lightly score the skull around the craniotomy with a scalpel, dry the area with cotton swabs, melt bone wax on a heated steel spatula, spread the wax over the scored skull and craniotomy, and allow 2–3 min for the wax to resolidify.

steps.title: Close scalp incision
steps.instruction: Suture the scalp using an interrupted suture pattern.

steps.title: Recover from anesthesia
steps.instruction: Remove ear bars, turn isoflurane flow to 0 %, continue heat support, swaddle the quail in a clean towel securing the wings, and hold until the bird is alert and responsive.

steps.title: Post‑operative housing
steps.instruction: Place the awake quail in a recovery cage with heat support (optional shroud to reduce stress) and monitor until fully mobile; then move to individual housing and perform daily health checks.

steps.title: Record surgical details
steps.instruction: Enter all relevant information (lesion type, intra‑operative problems, number of sutures, etc.) into the surgical log.

steps.title: Analyze FA behavior
steps.instruction: For each training day calculate mean latency to the target cup and number of choices; run a repeated‑measures ANOVA with lesion location as the between‑subject factor and training day as the within‑subject factor. For probe trials compare mean proximity to the baited cup versus the opposite cup with a paired t‑test; perform all analyses in JASP.

steps.title: Analyze SOR behavior
steps.instruction: Score exploration time when the bird is within 30 cm of an object (excluding preening or wall pecking); compute discrimination ratio DR = (N − F)/(N + F); compare mean DR across lesion groups with a one‑way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD post‑hoc; conduct all analyses in JASP.
